mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns in such regimes are not statistically different from a flat-rate model (p > 0.05) or the Fed rate cut within 3 months reverses the effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the monthly index of manufacturing production (INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength and slowing supply, both of which are associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by > 10% month-over-month while INDPRO falls by > 2% month-over-month
regime_hint: labor market softening coupled with supply contraction
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the correlation between the combined labor/supply signal and 20-day SPX returns is below -0.2 (weak negative effect).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 5% year-over-year for three consecutive months indicates accelerating household demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 10 such accelerated months, the average 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production (INDPRO) to capacity utilization (implied via a high GDPC1) falls by more than 4 percentage points in a month, it reflects underutilized capacity and suggests a supply-side slack that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO / (GDPC1/100) drops by >4pp in a single month
failure_condition: The interaction signal is not significant in a Granger causality test (p > 0.10) or 20-day returns are not consistently negative when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative return in the 60-day window following the trigger, or the FEDFUNDS response is absent within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% (UNRATE < 4%) while monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) show accelerating growth (>5% MoM), it indicates a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and dampens equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
regime_hint: labor market tightening with strong hiring
failure_condition: The interaction is not predictive in a 12-month rolling forecast (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (implied by HOUST) of at least 8% over three months suggests weakening consumer demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Over 15 such months, the average 5-day return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the gap between industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP deflator (implied via GDPC1) widens by more than 6% in a quarter, it signals supply chain inflation or capacity misallocation that precedes S&P 500 volatility but does not consistently predict positive returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1/100 - INDPRO > 6% over the prior quarter
failure_condition: The interaction is not predictive of positive returns in 70% of triggered windows (binomial test p < 0.30).
